newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Hardy Oil looks to growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Hardy Oil looks to growth.

text.p: Hardy Oil and Gas Plc, having spent two years refocusing the company, is now embarking on a growth period which could lead to acquisitions this year, its chief executive said.

The company, which plans its biggest ever drilling programme this year and expects the go-ahead for some of its big developments, has agreed a new 200 million stg revolving bank credit facility to finance growth as well as acquisition opportunities.

'We've got the money to develop the oil projects, to fund the exploration programme and to grow the business, and that obviously will at some point involve us making acquisitions or (purchasing) assets,' John Walmsley told Reuters in a telephone interview.
With the company in the growth stage and with a good team in place, Walmsley said he would expect 'during the course of the year to put something on the books'.
Earlier, Hardy announced a net profit of 5.7 million stg in the nine months to December 31, 1996, against a loss of 6.6 million stg in the year to March 31, 1996.
Along with the 200 million stg credit facility, it had a 75.5 million stg balance from the end of 1996 -- putting Hardy in a strong position to finance growth.
The group plans total capital expenditure in 1997 of 80 million stg, of which around 20 million will be for exploration and appraisal.
'This represents a significant increase over the level of expenditure in previous years,' the company said in a statement accompanying the results.
Hardy plans 17 exploration and appraisal wells this year and is actively pursuing opportunities for growth in its core areas of the UK Continental Shelf, Australia and Pakistan, as well as India.

The Elgin/Franklin gas/condensate and Banff oilfields in the North Sea and the Main gas field in Pakistan are seen as having strong potential. Along with the offshore oilfield PY-3 in Pakistan and gas/condensate Bayu/Undan field in Australia, these developments are seen trebling Hardy's production over the next six years.
In Australia, where Hardy has an eight-well drilling programme, Walmsley expects news on the Bayu/Undan field in March or early April on who will operate it and how reserves will be allocated.
In India the company is operator of the PY-3 offshore oilfield with an 18 percent stake. Drilling is currently underway and Walmsley was hopeful it would produce oil in the second half of the year.
Hardy has acquired a large 60 percent stake in the Ghotki gas concession and Walmsley said he is hopeful drilling will start there before the end of the year.

Asked if he could see the company as the target for a takeover bid, Walmsley said: 'Hardy at the moment is into its stride and that would not be in the slightest bit welcome or necessary as far as the company's progress is concerned'.
Walmsley takes the view that a firm oil price in 1997 would be a bonus but is not something to depend on.

The company has a 'terrifically strong balance sheet, we've now got the credit facility, our developments are pretty low cost developments per unit, so they're the strong core of the business -- if the price is weak, fine, we'll get on'.
